# Safety and efficacy of malaria vaccine candidate R21/Matrix-M in African children: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial
## Abstract
**Background:** Recently, we found that a new malaria vaccine, R21/Matrix-M, had over 75% efficacy against clinical malaria with seasonal administration in a phase 2b trial in Burkina Faso.
Here, we report on safety and efficacy of the vaccine in a phase 3 trial enrolling over 4800 children across four countries followed for up to 18 months at seasonal sites and 12 months at standard sites.

# **R21/Matrix-M™ Malaria Vaccine Phase 3 Trial Results Published in The Lancet**
Today, peer-reviewed results from a Phase 3 efficacy trial of the R21/Matrix-M™ malaria vaccine were published in _The Lancet_ . The trial was conducted across multiple sites in four African countries with 4,800 children aged 5-36 months.
Data from this trial served as the basis for the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recent prequalification of the R21/Matrix-M vaccine, paving the way for a global rollout that is expected to commence in mid-2024 by Serum Institute of India. answer: The R21/Matrix-M vaccine showed 79% efficacy against clinical malaria over 12 months at seasonal sites in children aged 5–17 months [1]. It showed 75% efficacy at standard sites for the same age group [1]. A phase 2b trial in Burkina Faso had over 75% efficacy with seasonal administration [1]. Published Phase 3 results report 75% efficacy when the vaccine is given before the high transmission season [3]. Published results report 68% efficacy with an age-based schedule in areas with perennial malaria [3]. The Phase 3 trial enrolled over 4800 children aged 5–36 months across four African countries [1].
